8709.t: Two theories: * According to Strong's Biblical Concordance, from χαράσσω (khărắssō, “to scratch; to inscribe”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰer- (“to scratch”) (compare Lithuanian žerti (“to scrape”)).

8704.t: From χύδην (khúdēn, “as if poured, in abundance”), adverb from the root of χέω (khéō, “to pour”) + -δην (-dēn), + -ιος (-ios, adjective suffix).

8720.t: Of unknown origin; possibly related to ψάω (psáō, “to rub, wipe”), and thus of Pre-Greek origin, though the morphology remains unclear if indeed related.

8744.t: From ἀγωνίζομαι (agōnízomai, “I contend for a prize”) + -τής (-tḗs, masculine agentive suffix).

8710.t: From χάσκω (khắskō, “to yawn; to gape”) + -μα (-mă, result noun suffix).

8705.t: Traditionally derived as a nominal formation from χέω (khéō, “to pour”), but like χυμός (khūmós, “juice, liquid”), it is unclear how the long -υ- (-ū-) can be explained.

8727.t: Traditionally compared to Sanskrit प्साति॑ (psā́ti, “to chew, eat, devour”) and explained as vocalic enlargements from Proto-Indo-European *bʰes-, found in Sanskrit बभ॑स्ति (bábhasti, “to chew, devour”).

8728.t: Unknown. Like ψεῦδος (pseûdos) and ψύθος (psŭ́thos), it may originally be onomatopoeic and somehow belong with the interjection ψό (psó).

8746.t: From earlier *ἀδϝεές (*adweés). By surface analysis, ἀ- (ă-, “not”) + δείδω (deídō, “to fear”) + -ής (-ḗs, adjectival suffix).

8799.t: Presumably from λάω (láō, “to see”), although a privative formation should have barytone accentuation.

8776.t: Often cited as borrowed from Iranian, compared to Sogdian 𐼸𐼷𐼻𐼰𐼸 (kynʾk /⁠kīnak, kēnak⁠/, “sword”), though this etymology is disputed.

8711.t: Pisani unsuccessfully attempted to link the word to κριθή (krithḗ, “barley”). According to Beekes, it is a Pre-Greek word.

8717.t: Verbal adjective, from ψηλαφάω (psēlăphắō, “to feel, grope”) + -τός (-tós).

8754.t: From ἀ- (a-, “un”) + διάλυτος (diálutos, “that may be dissolved, loosened”)

8774.t: ἀ- (a-, “a-, un-”) + κατεργάζομαι (katergázomai, “to effect by labor, achieve”) + -τος (-tos, “adjectival suffix”).

8773.t: From ἀ- (a-, “a-, un-”) + καθίστημι (kathístēmi, “to set in order”) + -τος (-tos).
